To help turn that data into usable information, the {{variable.Report_FormAnswerReport}} converts raw query results into a structured format where columns represent questions and rows represent {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s. When an Event Organizer views the {{variable.Report_FormAnswerReport}}, they will see the following in a spreadsheet: * All {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}}s (responses) linked to the {{variable.Object_Event}}, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}, {{variable.Object_Session}}, or post-{{variable.Object_Event}} survey * {{variable.Object_Attendee}} details presented via a configurable {{variable.Object_Attendee}} field set Users can then tally responses, pull lists based on unique criteria, and segment {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s based on future needs. ## Set Up Reporting for Forms ### Prerequisites To change the “Blackthorn | Form Answer Report” field set, a user must have access to the following: * Salesforce Setup * {{variable.Object_Attendee}} object * Add Blackthorn packaged fields, Salesforce standard fields, and all custom fields ### Blackthorn | Form Answer Report Field Set The “Blackthorn | Form Answer Report” field set is available on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} object. Event Admins can use it to customize the fields included in the {{variable.Report_FormAnswerReport}}. Fields added to the field set will appear in the report’s far left column(s). * CreatedById * CreatedDate * Id * LastActivityDate * LastModifiedById * LastModifiedDate * Name * OwnerId * Go to Setup. 2. Click the Object Manager tab. 3. In the Quick Find box, enter and click “Event” (conference360__Event__c). 4. Click the Page Layouts tab. 5. Click the layout to which you want to add the quick action button. 6. Click Mobile & Lightning Actions. 7. Find **Form Answers Report** and drag and drop it onto the page. 8. Click {{variable.Button_Save}}. ## How it Works After a user clicks the **Form Answers Report** button, a report is generated, formatted, and emailed to the current user. The results or information visible in a report depend on the permissions/access of the user creating the report and fall into one of the following scenarios. ### Full Access If a user has access to all the data and generates a report, they will see the confirmation message and receive an email with a report, which will include all the column labels and data. ### Some Access If a user has access to some, but not all, of the data and generates a report, they will see the confirmation message and receive an email with a report, which will only include columns/data related to the objects/fields they have access to. ### No Access to the Data If a user doesn’t have access to any data in a report and generates a report, they will see the confirmation message and receive an email with the report. The attached report will only include the {{variable.Object_FormElement}}s (questions) as column headers and one {{variable.Object_Attendee}} per row, but the columns with data the user doesn’t have access to will be omitted. ### No Data If a user generates a report without data, they will see the confirmation message and receive an email with a blank report. ### Report Formatting for Multiple Forms If a user, who has access to all data points, generates a report that contains {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}}s (question responses) from an {{variable.Object_Event}}-level {{variable.Object_Form}}, two unique {{variable.Object_EventItem}}-level {{variable.Object_Form}}s, a post-{{variable.Object_Event}} {{variable.Object_Form}}, and a {{variable.Object_Form}} for a {{variable.Object_Session}} with only two {{variable.Object_SessionAttendee}}s… The report will be formatted with a {{variable.Object_FormElement}} (question) in each column as the header, and one row per {{variable.Object_Attendee}}. Each column also indicates which {{variable.Object_Form}} the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} came from. If a {{variable.Object_Form}}/{{variable.Object_FormElement}} does not apply to an {{variable.Object_Attendee}}, that cell will be blank. The {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s will be listed in the first row in the following order: {{variable.Object_Event}}, {{variable.Object_EventItem}}, {{variable.Object_Session}}, and post-{{variable.Object_Event}}. ## New Email Template The process of creating and sending a report to a user includes the “Blackthorn Formatted Form Response Report” {{variable.Object_EmailTemplate}}. The {{variable.Object_EmailTemplate}} includes the following text. Subject: “Your Blackthorn Form Response Report is Ready” Template description: “This email template is used as the automated delivery message when a user generates an attendee form response report via the quick action on the Event record in Salesforce.” Template body: ”The attendee form response report for [{{variable.Field_ETEvent_EventName}}] has been generated and is attached to this email as a CSV file. Report details: * Each row represents a single attendee. * Each column corresponds to a form question. * Only Attendee fields included in the configured Attendee field set are included alongside form data. * Data respects Salesforce user-level permissions; only accessible fields are included. If you did not initiate this report or have questions, please contact your system administrator. Please note that if the email report is empty, it is likely because no attendees have registered for your event.” ## Create a Report An {{variable.Object_Event}} must have one or more {{variable.Object_ET_FormSubmission}} responses to create a report. Clicking the **Form Answers Report** button creates a report with {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}}s for the {{variable.Object_Event}}. 1. Open an {{variable.Object_Event}} record. 2. In the drop-down navigation menu, click **Form Answers Report**. 3. Click **Generate Report**. The user will see the following message: “We are generating your report! We'll send it to [user email] when complete. Delivery time varies depending on the size of the event.” The user will receive an email with an attached report in .xls or .csv format. The report will include the following: * Columns represent questions and contain the {{variable.Object_FormElement}} labels. The {{variable.Object_FormSubmissionAnswer}}s appear left to right in the same order as the {{variable.Object_Attendee}} encounters them on the {{variable.Object_Attendee}}. * The first column contains {{variable.Object_Attendee}} fields from the field set. The {{variable.Object_Attendee}} {{variable.Field_Attendee_ID}} and {{variable.Field_Attendee_Name}} (Field Name: Name) are the default columns on the field set, but not on the report itself. * Rows represent {{variable.Object_Attendee}}s. * {{variable.Object_Attendee}} answers populate the intersecting cells (column x row).
